newsitem.title: USA: US senators say Weld likely to get hearing.
newsitem.headline: US senators say Weld likely to get hearing.

text.p: Chairman Jesse Helms may well grant a Foreign Relations Committee hearing for William Weld to be ambassador to Mexico to avoid being outflanked by dissidents, two Republican Senate colleagues said on Sunday.
The second-ranking Republican on the committee, Sen. Richard Lugar of Indiana, indicated on ABC-TV's "This Week" programme that he was willing to join an attempt to circumvent Helms.

Helms, a North Carolina Republican, has said he would not call a hearing on Weld, a Republican nominated by President Bill Clinton to be ambassador to Mexico. Weld resigned as governor of Massachusetts to pursue the post.
"My hope is Sen. Helms will surprise everybody and this week name a time," Lugar said.
"In due course, Gov. Weld needs to be heard," Lugar said. "I will try to play a role to see he does have a hearing and we can find out what he thinks about drugs, about Mexico."
Sen. James Imhofe, an Oklahoma Republican, expressed doubts about Weld's qualifications but said Helms probably would prefer to call a hearing than be outmanoeuvred.
"My expectation is Sen. Helms will call for a hearing," Imhofe said, appearing with Lugar on "This Week."
A White House official said the Clinton administration was still hopeful that support for Weld from both sides of the aisle will prompt Helms to change his mind.

"We certainly hope that bipartisan support for the Weld nomination will lead to a hearing because we believe that given an opportunity a solid majority of the Senate would vote to confirm Gov. Weld," spokesman Barry Toiv said.
Weld has accused Helms of autocratically refusing to let his nomination proceed. Helms contends Weld has a poor record on prevention of illegal drug use.

While Imhofe said "it's the chairman's perogative" to decide whether to act on an item of business, Lugar said the desires of committee members also must be given weight. The Weld-Helms row carried risk of a Republican "civil war," he said. Weld is a moderate, Helms a staunch conservative.
Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott refused on Thursday to try to force Helms to call a hearing. His advice to Weld was, "Accept consideration for another post or look for work."
